excerpt: Airbyte is an open-source data movement platform with 700+ connectors. Cloud plans from $20 a month, how credits work, and alternatives such as Fivetran.
content:
Airbyte is an open-source data movement platform. It copies data from the systems a business uses, such as databases, SaaS apps and files, into warehouses, data lakes, vector databases and AI agents, a pattern usually called ELT (extract, load, transform). Its homepage says it can run pipelines across 700+ connectors. It also pitches itself as a context layer for production AI agents: connected sources feed a queryable store so that agents can reason across systems without stitching APIs together at run time, and it offers an MCP Gateway for that purpose.

Airbyte was started by Michel Tricot, its CEO, and Jean Lafleur, its COO. Its About page says the two joined Y Combinator's W20 batch in January 2020 and built the first version between July and September 2020 with six connectors. The company now reports 700+ data replication connectors and 50+ agent connectors, 25,000 companies using Airbyte (including 20% of the Fortune 500), 2 million pipelines synced a day, more than 1,300 open-source contributors, 20,000+ GitHub stars and $181 million raised. Those figures are Airbyte's own.

Open source or cloud

You can run Airbyte yourself from its GitHub repository (Airbyte Core), or pay for the managed cloud. Cloud pricing is credit-based. Standard starts at $20 a month with 5 credits included and extra credits at $5 each; syncs can run at most once an hour and support is by portal without an SLA. Plus sells fixed monthly packages, from 40 credits for $189 up to 2,000 credits for $4,999, with SSO, 15-minute syncs, two workspaces and a 24-hour support SLA; overage is $5 a credit. Airbyte's own calculator notes that at 40 credits Plus ($189) works out cheaper than Standard ($195). Both have a 14-day free trial.

Pro and Enterprise Flex are priced by capacity, in "Data Workers" (dedicated compute units), rather than by volume, and are quoted by sales. Pro adds multiple workspaces, role-based access control and syncs as often as every five minutes; Enterprise Flex adds on-premises, multi-region and hybrid deployment, with Airbyte running the control plane while data stays inside your own boundary.

We have not tested Airbyte ourselves. This page brings together Airbyte's official site, its own announcements and reputable news coverage, plus the public pages of the products it is compared with, and says where each fact comes from.

use_cases: Sync SaaS, database and file data into a data warehouse or lake
Load documents into a vector database for an AI application
Give AI agents governed access to company data through connectors or the MCP Gateway
Run data pipelines on your own infrastructure with the open-source edition

fit: want an open-source option you can self-host and extend
need a long tail of connectors, including ones you build yourself
want predictable cloud costs through fixed credit packages (Plus)
not_fit: need syncs more often than hourly on the cheapest cloud plan (Standard is limited to one hour)
want enterprise support without a sales conversation: Pro and Enterprise Flex are quoted
have no one to operate it if you self-host

pros: Open-source core you can run for free on your own servers
700+ connectors, plus agent connectors and an MCP Gateway
Published cloud prices for Standard and Plus
cons: Standard cloud syncs at most hourly
Capacity-based Pro and Enterprise pricing is not published

pricing.intro: Airbyte's own prices, in US dollars per month.

plans.name: Open Source (Airbyte Core)
plans.detail: Run it yourself from the GitHub repository

plans.name: Standard
plans.detail: 5 credits included, extra credits $5 each; fully managed; max 1-hour sync frequency; portal support without SLA; 14-day trial

plans.name: Plus
plans.detail: Packages up to 2,000 credits for $4,999/month; SSO, 15-minute syncs, 2 workspaces, 24-hour support SLA; overage $5/credit; 14-day trial

plans.name: Pro
plans.detail: Capacity-based (Data Workers); multiple workspaces, SSO, RBAC, syncs up to every 5 minutes, premium support

plans.name: Enterprise Flex
plans.detail: Everything in Pro plus on-premises, multi-region and hybrid deployment with an Airbyte-managed control plane

alternatives.intro: Other data-integration tools. Descriptions come from each product's own site; Fivetran's prices are from its own pricing page.

items.name: Fivetran
items.what: Managed, automated data movement with 700+ connectors, now merged with dbt Labs
items.starts_at: Free plan up to 500,000 monthly active rows; then usage-based
items.difference: Fully managed and priced on monthly active rows; no self-hosted open-source edition.

items.name: Meltano
items.what: ETL platform for analytics engineers with 500+ connectors and flat pricing
items.difference: Also open-source rooted; pitches flat, predictable pricing.

items.name: Estuary
items.what: Right-time data platform that unifies CDC, streaming, batch and ETL pipelines
items.difference: Built around real-time change data capture and streaming.

faq.a: The open-source edition, Airbyte Core, is free to self-host. The managed cloud starts at $20 a month.

faq.q: How many connectors does Airbyte have?
faq.a: Airbyte says it has 700+ data replication connectors and 50+ agent connectors.

faq.q: How does Airbyte Cloud pricing work?
faq.a: Standard and Plus use credits: Standard starts at $20 a month with 5 credits; Plus sells monthly packages from 40 credits for $189. Pro and Enterprise Flex are priced by capacity and quoted by sales.
Michel Tricot (CEO) and Jean Lafleur (COO), who went through Y Combinator's W20 batch in 2020.
Airbyte has a self-hostable open-source edition and credit-based cloud plans; Fivetran is fully managed and priced on monthly active rows, with a free plan up to 500,000 rows.
